Tuning of an INLAvanilla fit

Source: R/control.R
vanilla_control.Rd

Builds the control list of inla_vanilla(): the limits of the mode search, of the VB correction and of the skew-normal scans. The defaults suit most fits. A plain list with some of these names works too, and is checked by the same rules: control = list(n_grid = 31) is control = vanilla_control(n_grid = 31).

Usage

vanilla_control(
  mode_maxit = 5000L,
  mode_maxeval = 5000L,
  mode_tol = 1e-10,
  vb_maxit = 25L,
  vb_tol = 0.001,
  vb_budget = 2,
  n_grid = 21L,
  log_threshold = -6,
  nlminb = list()
)

Arguments

mode_maxit, mode_maxeval

The most iterations, and evaluations of logpost, of the mode search by stats::nlminb() (its iter.max and eval.max). When the search stops short of the mode, it is restarted once, with each parameter scaled by its curvature and the same limits.

mode_tol

The relative tolerance of the mode search (the rel.tol of stats::nlminb()).

vb_maxit, vb_tol

The iteration limit and the convergence tolerance, in posterior SDs, of the fixed-point iteration of the VB correction, with vb_correction = "full" and when a one-step correction has to iterate. A step over 1.5 posterior SDs is cut to 1.5. With vb_correction = "full", if two steps in a row are cut, or it has not converged after vb_maxit steps, stats::nlminb() takes over. They also limit the solve that follows a failed check of a one-step correction, and a first step below vb_tol in every parameter is not checked.

vb_budget

The most that the default VB correction (vb_correction = "onestep") may spend when its check fails and it solves the VB equation, as a multiple of the calls that the mode and Hessian took. The sweeps of the correction, the two of the check among them, are capped at vb_budget times those calls over 2m + 1. The default of 2 lets the solve of most hard fits reach its root. A larger value, or Inf for no cap, lets it run on until vb_tol or vb_maxit, and 0 leaves a fit that fails the check at its mode. A fit that passes the check takes two sweeps whatever the value. See "The VB correction" in inla_vanilla().

n_grid

The number of points of each skew-normal scan, spread over \(\pm 4\) posterior SDs. At least 7.

log_threshold

Scan points whose log-posterior falls more than this below the maximum are left out of the skew-normal fit.

nlminb

A named list of any other controls of stats::nlminb() for the mode search, such as trace = 1, which prints its iterations, or abs.tol. Its iter.max, eval.max and rel.tol stand in for mode_maxit, mode_maxeval and mode_tol, which must then be left at their defaults. It does not reach the fallback optimiser of the VB correction or the conditional optimisations of marginal_scan = "laplace", which keep limits of their own.

Value

A list with an entry for each argument, for the control argument of inla_vanilla().

See also

inla_vanilla().

Examples

set.seed(1)
y <- rnorm(30, mean = 5, sd = 2)
logpost <- function(theta) {
  sigma <- exp(theta[["log_sigma"]])
  sum(dnorm(y, theta[["mu"]], sigma, log = TRUE)) +
    dnorm(theta[["mu"]], 0, 10, log = TRUE) +
    dexp(sigma, log = TRUE) + theta[["log_sigma"]]
}

# A finer scan of each marginal
fit <- inla_vanilla(
  logpost,
  c(mu = 0, log_sigma = 0),
  control = vanilla_control(n_grid = 41),
  silent = TRUE
)

# The same as a plain list
fit <- inla_vanilla(
  logpost,
  c(mu = 0, log_sigma = 0),
  control = list(n_grid = 41),
  silent = TRUE
)

# Print the iterations of the mode search
vanilla_control(nlminb = list(trace = 1))
#> $mode_maxit
#> [1] 5000
#> 
#> $mode_maxeval
#> [1] 5000
#> 
#> $mode_tol
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $vb_maxit
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> $vb_tol
#> [1] 0.001
#> 
#> $vb_budget
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $n_grid
#> [1] 21
#> 
#> $log_threshold
#> [1] -6
#> 
#> $nlminb
#> $nlminb$trace
#> [1] 1
#> 
#>
